content.overview: BNS s. 281 — Rash driving or riding on a public way.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Rash driving or riding on a public way. BNS restatement of IPC 279. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 279. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 281 is the rule on “Rash driving or riding on a public way”. The section provides that whoever drives any vehicle, or rides, on any public way in a manner so rash or negligent as to endanger human life, or to be likely to cause hurt or injury to any other person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 281 exists so that “Rash driving or riding on a public way” has a closed legal test in Chapter XV — Of Offences Affecting the Public Health, Safety, Convenience, Decency and Morals. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Nuisance, adulteration, rash driving, obscenity, lottery.

hypotheticals.question: Whether BNS s. 281 (Rash driving or riding on a public way) applies, and how structured written arguments should be framed.
hypotheticals.analysis:
Step 1 — Identify the provision. The correct current-law cite is BNS s. 281 (Rash driving or riding on a public way), Chapter XV — Of Offences Affecting the Public Health, Safety, Convenience, Decency and Morals.
Step 2 — State the legal test in your own words, then list the ingredients:
   (1) Whoever drives any vehicle, or rides, on any public way in a manner so rash or negligent as to endanger human life, or to be likely to cause hurt or injury to any other person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both
Step 3 — Check limitations, provisos and the rest of the Chapter so you do not apply s. 281 in a vacuum.
Step 4 — Map each fact to an ingredient. Write “this fact proves ingredient (a)” or “this fact is missing, so the section is not made out”.
Step 5 — Conclude. If every essential ingredient is proved and no exception covers the case, BNS s. 281 applies. If any essential ingredient fails, say so and stop. Do not invent a different section to save the answer.
